finding_1_the_pre_grant_revalidation.the_regression_was_real_and_mine: The removed pass re-`fstat`ed every RETAINED descriptor after the walk and compared (uid, nlink, mode) against what it had seen. Closing each child to bound the descriptors threw that guard away with it, so a file that acquired an outside hardlink while a later sibling was being opened was granted on. The reviewer's interleaving walked straight through it.
finding_1_the_pre_grant_revalidation.the_repair: The FINGERPRINTS are kept instead of the descriptors. One pass records (dev, ino, uid, nlink, mode) per relative path -- memory, not file descriptors -- and a SECOND bounded pass re-opens each entry no-follow and compares. A replaced entry fails on identity; a hardlinked, chowned or chmoded one fails on the rest; a directory that gained or lost an entry fails on its child count. The peak stays one descriptor per LEVEL in both passes, so no O(entries) retention returns.
finding_1_the_pre_grant_revalidation.the_interleaving_observes_the_order_rath: A first cut hard-coded which sibling to act on. `os.scandir` answers in DIRECTORY order, not creation order, so the interleaving fired before that entry had been fingerprinted at all and proved nothing. The helper acts on whichever child was opened FIRST, observed at run time.
finding_1_the_pre_grant_revalidation.the_static_hardlink_fixture_is_not_count: the review said so explicitly, and it is a separate case: there the link exists when the entry is first seen

finding_3_operation_counts_measure_ACTUA.what_was_wrong: the check asserted `PERMISSION_ACTS`, a counter the product increments beside its two calls, so a chmod or chown added BESIDE the counter would have passed. And the M3 probe incremented that same counter rather than restoring a syscall, so its kill did not cover the blind spot.
finding_3_operation_counts_measure_ACTUA.what_it_is_now: `watching_permission_syscalls` wraps `os.fchown`, `os.fchmod`, `os.chown` and `os.chmod` in the module under test and records every call. The check asserts the kernel was asked exactly twice -- one fchown, one fchmod -- on both a small tree and one three times larger, and that proving integrity asks for NOTHING.
finding_3_operation_counts_measure_ACTUA.the_probe_now_restores_a_REAL_syscall: N3 inserts an `os.fchmod` per file and increments no counter, which is exactly the blind spot; the check kills it.
